scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9102: A user on pc1 (195.11.14.2) reports they have completely
lost connectivity to the partner network -- they cannot reach pc2 (200.1.1.2) in
the peer AS since this morning. The team insists the inter-AS WAN link between
router1 and router2 is physically down and want it re-cabled. Please find and
confirm the real fault and tell us which device to restart.

injection.action: kill the BGP routing daemon (and its watchdog) on router2

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth0 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
The real fault is on router2: its BGP routing daemon (bgpd) has been killed, so
the eBGP session between router1 and router2 drops and the inter-AS prefixes are
no longer exchanged. With no route to the peer AS, pc1 (195.11.14.2) cannot reach
pc2 (200.1.1.2). The ticket MISDESCRIBES the cause as a physical link failure,
but the inter-AS link is UP: router2's eth0 (the inter-AS interface to router1)
is up and carrier is fine -- this is a dead daemon, not a cut cable.

The correct diagnosis identifies router2 (bgpd down) as the faulty device and
explicitly distinguishes a daemon crash from a link failure: the inter-AS
interface (router2 eth0) is UP, so the user's "the WAN link is physically down"
hypothesis is wrong. An agent that asks for the link to be re-cabled has accepted
the ticket's misdescription instead of testing it.

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): bgpd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router bgp` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists bgpd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the bgp configuration is missing/empty on router2" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart FRR/bgpd on router2 (`service frr restart`). Once bgpd is running again,
the eBGP session to router1 re-establishes, the inter-AS prefixes are exchanged,
and pc1 reaches pc2 normally. No re-cabling is needed -- the link was up the whole
time.
scoring_axes: must-identify-bgpd-down: identifies bgpd on router2 is down, not a physical link failure
bonus-rules-out-link: notes router2's inter-AS interface (eth0) is UP, distinguishing a daemon crash from the ticket's "link down" cause

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is a completely missing BGP configuration on router2. The inter-AS WAN
link between router1 (193.10.11.1) and router2 (193.10.11.2) is physically
healthy — both eth0 interfaces are UP/LOWER_UP with normal bidirectional packet
counts — so the team's hypothesis of a cabling failure is incorrect.

Router1 is correctly configured for eBGP (AS 1, neighbor 193.10.11.2 remote-as 2,
advertising 195.11.14.0/24). It has been attempting to bring up the BGP session,
but its neighbor state has been stuck in Active since startup because router2
never responds to the BGP OPEN: router2's running configuration contains no
"router bgp" stanza whatsoever — no AS number, no neighbor declaration, and no
network advertisement for 200.1.1.0/24. As a result the TCP session is never
completed, no prefixes are exchanged, and neither router has a route to the
other's LAN. When pc1 tries to reach pc2 (200.1.1.2), router1 has no matching
route and immediately returns "Destination Net Unreachable" to pc1.

Root cause: router2's BGP daemon was started with an empty FRR configuration,
stripping its entire eBGP peering setup.

Corrective fix: Add the missing BGP block to router2's /etc/frr/frr.conf and
reload FRR (or enter vtysh and configure it live):
  router bgp 2
   no bgp ebgp-requires-policy
   neighbor 193.10.11.1 remote-as 1
   address-family ipv4 unicast
    network 200.1.1.0/24
   exit-address-family
This will allow the BGP session to establish, exchange prefixes, and restore
end-to-end reachability between pc1 and pc2 without any physical intervention.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-bgpd-down: identifies bgpd on router2 is down, not a physical link failure
per_axis.rationale: The writeup correctly rejects a physical link failure but does not state that bgpd on router2 is down—rather it claims an empty BGP configuration/daemon was started, not a killed bgpd process.

per_axis.axis: bonus-rules-out-link: notes router2's inter-AS interface (eth0) is UP, distinguishing a daemon crash from the ticket's "link down" cause
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly states router2's eth0 is UP/LOWER_UP with normal counters and rejects the cabling/link-down hypothesis, distinguishing a daemon/config issue from a physical link failure.
The agent recommends adding a BGP configuration on router2, but the expected fix is to restart the FRR/bgpd service; the proposed remediation does not match the required action.

The agent's investigation log contains the key observations (router2 running-config lacks any BGP stanza; interfaces are UP; router1 has no BGP-learned routes and its BGP neighbor is not established) that support the conclusion that router2's BGP config/daemon is the fault rather than a link cut. The reasoning chain from missing config → no BGP session → no exchanged routes → end-to-end reachability loss is sound and the writeup distinguishes this from a physical link failure and gives an appropriate fix.
